blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
In the UK, people often say less than they mean. When a British colleague says "that's an interesting idea", they may really mean "I don't agree at all." When they say "not bad", they often mean "really good."

This is not dishonest. It is a style. The British like to soften strong words. They leave part of the meaning in the tone or in the context.

For newcomers, this can be confusing. For everyone, it is a good habit to learn. When you read the tone and the context, you understand what people really mean.

items.q: When a British colleague says "that's an interesting idea", what may they really mean?
items.why: "they may really mean 'I don't agree at all'" — a frase é educada, mas discorda.

items.q: What does "not bad" often mean in British English?
items.why: "'not bad', they often mean 'really good'".

items.q: According to the text, this style is…
items.why: "This is not dishonest. It is a style."

items.q: The text suggests that, to understand a British colleague, you should…
options: listen to the tone and the context too
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que parte do sentido está no tom e no contexto, não só nas palavras.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which idea?
options: British people leave part of the meaning in the tone.
"Not bad" can be a good thing.
The British are dishonest when they soften words.
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma claramente que isso NÃO é desonesto — é um estilo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte explicar a uma colega nova o que o gerente britânico quis dizer. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, come in and sit down. You asked me about the meeting yesterday. Yes, I can help. Your manager is British, and British people often say less than they mean.

When he said your report was "not bad", that is very good news. "Not bad" often means "really good" here. He was happy with your work. Do not worry about that.

But listen to this part too. He said "perhaps we could look at the numbers again." That word "perhaps" is soft, but the message is not soft. He wants you to check the numbers. It is not really a question.

And when he said "that's an interesting idea", be careful. Sometimes that means he does not agree. It is a polite way to say no.

So my advice is simple. Listen to the words, but also read the tone and the context. In Brazil people are more direct, and that is fine. Here, the meaning is often between the lines. You will learn it fast. Just ask me when you are not sure.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Charlotte say about "not bad"?
options: It means the report is late
It means the report is short
items.why: "'Not bad' often means 'really good' here. He was happy with your work."

items.q: When the manager said "perhaps we could look at the numbers again", Charlotte says he…
options: does not care about the numbers
really wants you to check the numbers
items.why: "He wants you to check the numbers. It is not really a question."

items.q: What can "that's an interesting idea" sometimes mean?
items.why: "Sometimes that means he does not agree. It is a polite way to say no."

items.q: Why does Charlotte mention Brazil?
options: To say Brazilian people are more direct
To say the report is about Brazil
To say the meeting was in Brazil
To say the manager is Brazilian
items.why: Inferência: ela compara — "In Brazil people are more direct" — para explicar a diferença de estilo.

items.q: How would you best describe Charlotte's tone with the new colleague?
items.why: Inferência: ela tranquiliza ("Do not worry") e oferece ajuda ("Just ask me") — é acolhedora.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The British often soften strong words." To soften means to…
items.why: Soften = suavizar, tornar mais gentil.

items.q: "His answer was very indirect." Indirect means…
items.why: Indirect = indireto, não direto ao ponto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She is new here, so she is still a ___."
items.why: Newcomer = recém-chegado, quem acabou de entrar.

items.q: "To understand him, you must read between the lines." This means…
items.why: Read between the lines = ler nas entrelinhas, captar o sentido escondido.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The difference was small and hard to see — it was very ___."
items.why: Subtle = sutil, difícil de perceber.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de trabalho. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the report." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "They will roll out the new plan next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar aos poucos.

items.q: "She pushed back on the idea in a polite way." She…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar de forma educada.

items.q: "He said yes, but he never followed through." He…
options: did not finish what he promised
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "When you are not sure, read between the lines." This means…
items.why: Read between the lines = ler nas entrelinhas, buscar o sentido não dito.
